World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). These will allow investment assets such as shares and investment fund units to be exempt from the 19% capital gains tax up to a limit of 100,000 zloty. Of this amount, up to 25,000 zloty may be held in savings assets such as bonds and deposits. Assets held in an OKI above those limits will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱 — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026 The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK). However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age. Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%. By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and who Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has only a majority of nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the re-introduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. World.title: Poland says it foiled Russian plot to “execute” US-Ukrainian citizen in Warsaw

Poland has detained a Russian national who it says was planning to assassinate a person with joint US and Ukrainian citizenship in Warsaw. The news was first announced by Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a press conference on Thursday afternoon. “Thanks to the truly brilliant action of our security services – the Internal Security Agency (ABW) with the assistance of the police – on 7 August we detained a Russian citizen, recruited by Russian intelligence services, whose task was to execute an American and Ukrainian citizen right here in Warsaw,” he said. “This is the first time someone on Russian orders has decided to attack an American citizen on the territory of another NATO country,” added Tusk. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: 7 sierpnia zatrzymaliśmy obywatela Rosji, którego zadaniem było wykonanie egzekucji w Warszawie na obywatelu amerykańskim i ukraińskim równocześnie. Dzięki akcji ABW i Policji udało się temu zapobiec. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Though the prime minister said he was not allowed to name either the suspect or the target, he revealed that the latter was someone who is “inconvenient for Putin’s regime”. Tusk also gave no details of how the assassination was supposed to have been carried out, but said that it was foiled “at the last minute”. In a subsequent statement, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of Poland’s security services, confirmed Tusk’s announcement and noted that the operation to prevent the attack had taken place in cooperation with the US. Police headquarters in Warsaw later revealed that the 29-year-old suspect had been charged with planning a murder and accepting an order to carry out murder in return for material or personal benefit. Both crimes carry jail terms of between two and 15 years. He has also been placed in court-approved pretrial detention. 7 sierpnia br. ABW we współpracy z policją zatrzymała obywatela Rosji, który na zlecenie obcej służby przygotowywał zabójstwo obywatela USA ukraińskiego pochodzenia. Do zabójstwa miało dojść w Warszawie. Operacja była realizowana we współpracy ze służbami USA. — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) August 13, 2026 Poland has been a major target for hostile operations by agents working on behalf of Russia. In February, a report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism found that Poland is the most frequently targeted country in a campaign of sabotage being orchestrated by Russia across Europe. That included an attempt last year to use explosives to derail a train. In June, a Russian artist whose work criticised Putin was assassinated in Poland. Soon after, the Polish security services detained the suspected killer, who they said was using a Georgian passport. Last month, a Russian missile hit Poland during intensive attacks on Ukraine. That followed an incident last year in which around 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace. Poland has also been one of Ukraine’s closest allies since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, providing significant military, humanitarian and diplomatic support, as well as welcoming millions of Ukrainian refugees, almost one million of whom remain in Poland. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland hit by theft of 19 million patients’ data from medical platform

We cannot do what we do without your support. The personal data of almost 19 million people, including medical information, has been compromised in a major cyberattack on a company that provides services to thousands of medical facilities in Poland. “We are dealing with one of the largest incidents in Poland’s history,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski on Wednesday. He urged people to use government services to check whether their data is affected and to “lock” their national identity number to prevent potential fraud. (￼🧵 1/2) 💬 Dziś doszło do poważnego wycieku danych w firmie MyDr, który może obejmować blisko 19 milionów osób korzystających z opieki medycznej. W związku z sytuacją krytyczną zostały natychmiast podjęte działania mające zabezpieczyć dane i wyjaśnić okoliczności incydentu –… pic.twitter.com/nIp6EvbKiu — Ministerstwo Cyfryzacji (@CYFRA_GOV_PL) August 12, 2026 The attack targeted MyDr, a company that provides services used by many medical facilities in Poland. Its data includes patients’ personal information, as well as medical details such as diagnoses and prescriptions. It was first reported on Monday by Zaufana Trzecia Strona, an IT security news service, which said that it had been contacted on Saturday by the alleged perpetrators, who claimed to have accessed the data of around 18.8 million people. The hackers, who have not been identified, had also sent a screenshot from the compromised database showing the personal data of “one of the most important politicians in Poland”, added Zaufana Trzecia Strona. Shortly afterwards, MyDr confirmed that it had “become the target of an external, deliberate criminal activity involving some of our data”. In an update on Wednesday, it said that, at the time of writing, there was no evidence that the data had been published anywhere. He noted that “there is no indication we are dealing with an external attack…from Russia or any other country”. Poland has recently regularly been targetted by Russian state-linked hackers. It is “very likely” that cybercriminals are behind the attack on MyDr, said Gawkowski, who pledged that there would be an “uncompromising” response from the Polish security services. The minister advised Poles to check in a secure government database whether their data had been leaked. He also advised citizens to use the state web portal, known as mObywatel, to “lock” their identity number, known as a PESEL, which prevents fraudsters from using it. Around 12,000 medical facilities use MyDr’s services, the digital affairs ministry told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). World.title: Passenger Attacks Four Airport Staff After Being Denied Boarding in Prague
World.content:
A passenger attacked four employees of ground-handling company Menzies Aviation at Prague’s Airport on Thursday evening after being denied boarding on a flight to Rome.

The incident took place at Terminal 2, near Gate C9, shortly after 8 p.m., according to Zdopravy.cz.

The woman arrived late for boarding on a Ryanair flight. After being refused entry to the aircraft, she reportedly became aggressive and attacked members of the ground-handling staff.



One of the employees stepped between the woman and a colleague who was being confronted by her. The passenger then bit him.

Airport police were called to the scene and used restraint equipment to detain the woman. She was subsequently escorted from the boarding area and handed over to the Czech police.

“The woman was late for the boarding gate, and after being denied boarding, she physically attacked an airport employee,” Josef Urban, a spokesperson for the Foreign Police Directorate said.

“Responding officers detained her using restraint equipment, and the case is now being investigated as disorderly conduct,” he added.

The incident was also confirmed by Prague Airport spokesperson Jiří Hánich.

The injured employees required medical treatment following the attack. Four members of the Menzies team were reportedly involved in the incident.

Menzies Aviation has operated at Václav Havel Airport Prague since 1991. The company provides ground-handling services covering passengers, baggage, aircraft and cargo for a significant share of flights at the airport.

World.title: Around 300 Czech Citizens Evacuated Due to Fire in Croatia
World.content:
Some 300 Czech tourists are among the 1,000 evacuees with a Czech police officer sent to coordinate the emergency response.

Croatian prime minister Andrej Plenković is in the town holding a coordination meeting with all emergency services this morning. Croatian president Zoran Milanović is also expected later today.

“All those injured in last night’s fire are being provided with the necessary medical care,” Plenković said in an earlier update on X.

No fatalities have been reported. The spokesman said there were also no reports of serious injuries among Czech citizens.

Some tourists left the area on their own, while others are staying at evacuation centres in Omiš and Split. A Czech consul is on site and is in contact with local authorities and security forces.

Fire spreads across up to 1,000 hectares

Around 160 firefighters, supported by specialised firefighting aircraft, are battling the blaze.

The fire has caused significant material damage, according to eyewitnesses, with dozens of cars and homes reportedly destroyed. Strong winds have helped the flames spread across an area estimated at between 900 and 1,000 hectares.

Witnesses reported hearing gas cylinders exploding inside burning homes, while the streets were filled with the sirens of fire engines, ambulances and police vehicles. Large parts of Omiš have also been left without electricity.

Mass evacuation underway

Hundreds of people have fled the affected area, with some tourists escaping by boat, catamaran and other small vessels.

The organised evacuation is being coordinated through the Ribnjak sports hall in Omiš. From there, evacuees are being transported by bus to the Gripe sports centre in Split.

According to Omiš fire chief Slavko Tucaković, foreigners make up the majority of those evacuated.

World.title: Czech Villages Face Water Shortages as Drought Deepens
World.content:
Residents say they are cutting water use wherever possible, taking shorter showers, reducing garden watering and abandoning plans to fill swimming pool.

Communities across the Czech Republic are struggling with worsening water shortages as wells dry up and small streams disappear after years of increasingly severe drought, according to local media on Thursday.



In the village of Krsy in the Plzen Region, tankers are delivering drinking water daily to a reservoir above the village. Some private wells have already run dry, while others are close to empty.

Residents said they are cutting water use wherever possible, taking shorter showers, reducing garden watering and abandoning plans to fill swimming pools.

Authorities are urging households to connect to public water networks where available.

The shortages are also putting pressure on tourist destinations. In Horni Becva, in the Beskydy Mountains, the population doubles during the summer holidays.

The municipality’s two wells have been operating close to their limits, with firefighters called in to deliver water.

Hotels with wellness facilities are among the largest users, prompting local officials to ask businesses to reduce consumption.

Officials hope conditions will improve when the tourist season ends and autumn rains arrive.

World.title: Burgermeister to Open First Prague Restaurant on Wenceslas Square in 2027
World.content:
Berlin burger chain Burgermeister is preparing to enter the Czech market, with its first Prague restaurant expected to open in early 2027.

The company has chosen Wenceslas Square for its debut. The location will also serve as a base for Burgermeister’s planned expansion across the Czech Republic, with more restaurants already in the pipeline.

Burgermeister has built its reputation in Berlin over the past two decades, growing from a single restaurant in a former public toilet into an international chain with 32 locations across Germany and other European markets.



Burgermeister has not yet revealed the exact address or confirmed a specific opening date.

The Prague restaurant will follow the concept that made Burgermeister popular in Berlin. The chain focuses on freshly prepared burgers and fries, with part of its food production handled in-house. Its operations also include its own bakery.

From a former public toilet to an international burger chain

Burgermeister opened its first restaurant in the Kreuzberg district of Berlin in 2006. The location was far from a conventional restaurant site. It occupied a former public toilet beneath the railway tracks near Schlesisches Tor station.

The unusual setting quickly became part of the brand’s identity. Over the years, Burgermeister expanded beyond its original Berlin location and developed into a larger restaurant chain.

Today, the company has 32 branches and is pursuing its goal of building a pan-European network.

World.title: This Website Tracks How Many Trams Are Still Running Without Air Conditioning
World.content:
A new website is giving Prague residents a live picture of how many trams are operating without air conditioning, highlighting an issue that has become particularly noticeable during the city’s summer heat.

The service, Smrdime.cz, was created by developer Christoph Korb. Its name is a play on the Czech word smrdíme, meaning “we stink,” and refers to the uncomfortable conditions passengers can face inside overheated trams.

The website uses live data to calculate the share of Prague’s trams that are currently running without air conditioning. The figures change throughout the day as new vehicles enter and leave service.

When the service was checked on Thursday, August 13, Prague was experiencing temperatures of around 37 degrees Celsius. At that point, 188 of the 256 trams in operation did not have air conditioning, representing about 71 percent of the fleet being tracked.



Of the 147 air-conditioned trams available, 77 were operating at the same time.

The figures provide a snapshot rather than a fixed daily total. As trams are taken out of service and replaced, the balance between air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned vehicles changes continuously.

The project draws attention to a long-standing issue facing Prague’s public transport system: a substantial part of the city’s tram fleet still lacks air conditioning.

The website is based on data from two publicly available sources. Transport information comes from Golemio, Prague’s open-data platform, while weather information is provided by Open-Meteo. The two data sources are used to calculate the current situation displayed on the site.

Korb built the service with Anthropic’s Claude Code development tool. He has also published the project’s source code on GitHub, allowing other developers to inspect the project and contribute to its development.

World.title: From a Student’s Dream to a Japanese Bakery in Prague: The Story Behind Yaki-Pan
World.content:
For Hoan, opening a bakery in Prague was not a sudden business idea. It was a dream that had been taking shape for more than a decade.

After arriving in Prague as a student, Hoan watched members of the Vietnamese community build businesses across the city, most commonly in restaurants, grocery shops and nail salons.

She worked in grocery stores and restaurants herself, gradually gaining experience in the food industry while studying.

But after finishing school, she still was not sure what kind of business she wanted to open.



One thing was clear: she loved baking.

“Its my dream. It’s been my plan for a long time, more than 10 years,” she says.

Rather than opening another coffee shop, she decided to focus on what she knew best. She had visited bakeries around Prague and noticed what she saw as a gap in the city’s food scene: there were few places specialising in Japanese-style baking.

Around six years ago, she decided that she wanted to fill that gap herself.

The result was Yaki-Pan, a small bakery built around Japanese pastries and flavours. Before opening, Hoan spent roughly a year and a half — and much of that time at home — testing recipes and trying to recreate the textures and flavours she associated with Japanese baking.

Getting there was not straightforward.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Yaki-Pan (@yakipan_brunch)

Learning to work with Czech ingredients

For Hoan, authenticity was essential. She wanted the pastries at Yaki-Pan to resemble Japanese baked goods as closely as possible, but she quickly discovered that one of the most important ingredients presented a major challenge: flour.

Japanese flour differs significantly from the flour commonly available in the Czech Republic. The differences affect the texture, consistency and ultimately the finished pastry.

“The flour here is not the same as when I learnt,” she says.

Instead of simply following recipes she had learned elsewhere, Hoan had to adapt them to local ingredients. She experimented with different combinations of flour and spent months trying to achieve the texture she was looking for.

Three years ago, she travelled to China to study Japanese baking under professionals. There, she was able to work with Japanese ingredients and gain further experience. Returning to Europe meant starting another process of adjustment.

She considered importing Japanese flour to the Czech Republic, but eventually found it difficult to maintain as a long-term solution. Instead, she continued experimenting with locally available ingredients.

“I needed to test for about two years at my home,” she says.

The process has not necessarily ended with the bakery’s opening. Hoan continues to work on her recipes and ingredients, looking for ways to improve the pastries while staying as close as possible to the style she wants to create.

A warm welcome from Prague

If Hoan was worried that Japanese flavours might be unfamiliar to Prague customers, the first day quickly put those concerns to rest.

When Yaki-Pan opened, she had not prepared significantly more food than usual. Within 30 minutes, the bakery had sold out.

The first two months were particularly busy, especially at weekends. Today, the customer base includes tourists, Japanese residents and visitors who have become regulars.

Japanese customers have also played an important role in validating Hoan’s approach, frequently complimenting her on how closely the pastries resemble those they know from Japan.

Among the most popular items is shio-pan, a Japanese-style bread known for its soft texture and salty flavour. At Yaki-Pan, the vegan version has become one of the bakery’s bestsellers and regularly sells out.

Hoan’s own favourite pastry, meanwhile, changes from day to day.

The bakery’s success has also brought an unexpected question. Some customers have asked why a Vietnamese woman decided to open a Japanese bakery.

For Hoan, the answer is simple. “It’s my dream,” she says. “I put all my energy into my recipes.”

Her background, she suggests, is less important than the work she has put into learning the craft and developing the food.

Building Yaki-Pan’s future

For now, Hoan is focused on the bakery she has already built. Yaki-Pan is run by Hoan and her husband, and her previous experience working in restaurants has helped her manage the busy days herself.

The couple are already thinking about the next stage. They hope to add outdoor seating next year and, eventually, open another location.

But there is no immediate rush to expand.

“Now I want to put all my energy into this one,” Hoan says.

There are also plans to introduce another type of matcha, giving customers more choice alongside the bakery’s existing drinks.

For a business that began as an idea Hoan carried with her for more than 10 years, Yaki-Pan remains very much a work in progress. The recipes continue to evolve, customers continue to discover Japanese-style baking, and Hoan is still searching for the ingredients and techniques that bring her original vision closest to reality.

World.title: Prague Taxi Driver Arrested After Taking CZK 3.5 Million Left in His Car
World.content:
A 21-year-old taxi driver in Prague has been arrested after allegedly taking a suitcase containing CZK 3.5 million in cash that passengers accidentally left in his car.

The money was recovered by police after the driver eventually admitted what he had done and told investigators where he had hidden it. He now faces up to five years in prison.

The incident happened in late July, although police only released details of the case several days later.



The passengers were a married couple who had taken a taxi to Václav Havel Airport in the early morning. They were heading on vacation and only realized after reaching the airport that one of their suitcases was still in the vehicle.

The couple immediately contacted the driver and asked him to bring the suitcase back. According to police, he initially agreed, but the luggage never appeared despite further calls and reminders.

The couple eventually reported the matter to police. Given the amount of money involved, forensic specialists from the Prague 1 police precinct joined the investigation.

Investigators quickly located the taxi and detained the driver. A search of the vehicle, however, produced no suitcase.

The 21-year-old initially denied that the passengers had left anything behind, telling police that he had not found any luggage in the car.

His account later changed.

After being placed in a cell, the man confessed and revealed where he had hidden the cash. Police officers and forensic specialists then located the money in a forest near Kladno.

The investigation also uncovered an attempt to destroy evidence. Near the cash, investigators found the burned remains of the suitcase. Police say the driver had taken the items to the forest, piled them together and set them on fire.

The driver remains under investigation and could face a prison sentence of up to five years if convicted.

World.title: Six Prague Rooftops and Terraces to Visit Before Summer Ends
World.content:
Summer is already moving on, and Prague’s rooftop season won’t last much longer.

August is the time to make the most of the city’s terraces, sunset views and outdoor events before they disappear for another year.

Here are six rooftops and terraces worth visiting before autumn arrives.



1. REASON at Masaryčka

Eleven floors above Masaryk Station, REASON offers one of Prague’s newest rooftop dining spots, with views over the city and the Zaha Hadid-designed Masaryčka development.

This summer, its terrace is also home to the seasonal Frerejean Frères Champagne Bar, serving champagne by the glass, cocktails, oysters and light bites. The menu includes THE REASON KIR, made with herbs grown on the rooftop.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and cocktails above Masaryčka.

2. W Prague – ABOVE Rooftop

ABOVE Rooftop at W Prague brings a Mediterranean feel to the top of Wenceslas Square.

The daily Mediterranean Hour runs from 5 to 6 PM, with two spritzes and a Taste of the Mediterranean platter for CZK 990. Oysters are also served from Thursday to Saturday, alongside a programme of summer events and pop-ups.

This summer: Mediterranean Hour, sunset drinks and oysters in the centre.

3. MINUTY Rooftop Terrace

The rooftop at Fairmont Golden Prague offers views across Pařížská, Letná and the city centre from nine floors up.

MINUTY Rooftop Terrace by Golden Eye focuses on champagne, oysters, caviar and cocktails. The terrace is seasonal and is expected to remain open until September, weather permitting.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and caviar with a view.

4. Sky Lounge 360°

For the view alone, Sky Lounge 360° is hard to beat. The rooftop looks across Prague’s historic centre and becomes livelier during the summer months, with DJs, sunset events and Prague Rooftop Festival activities.

It is more about drinks and atmosphere than a long dinner — a good option for an evening that starts at sunset and continues after dark.

This summer: Sunset events, DJs and panoramic views.

5. Casablanca Sky Bar

On the sixth floor of The President Hotel, Casablanca Sky Bar looks out over the Vltava and Prague skyline.

With DJs, cocktails and regular sunset events, it has more of a party atmosphere than a traditional hotel rooftop. It is also one of the venues taking part in the Prague Rooftop Festival.

This summer: DJs, cocktails and sunset parties above the Vltava.

6. Monkey Bar

Monkey Bar at Falkensteiner Hotel Prague is a quieter alternative, with a green, jungle-style terrace close to the main railway station.

Every Thursday until the end of August, the terrace hosts BBQ & Beats, combining barbecue, live music and summer drinks. Frozen margaritas are also on the menu.

For daytime plans, there is Jungle Brunch, including a bottomless mimosa option.

This summer: BBQ & Beats every Thursday through August.

World.title: Sinking barges are already raising the Danube at Paks before reaching the riverbed
World.content:
Hungary’s emergency operation to raise the Danube’s water level near the Paks Nuclear Power Plant has produced its first encouraging result, even before the two barges being sunk in the river have reached the bottom.

The two 80-metre barges were positioned across the Danube as part of the emergency intervention designed to slow the river and raise water levels at the power plant’s cold-water intake. According to Gyula Kovács, the local technical coordinator of Hungary’s water management authority, simply positioning the barges across the river has already created a small damming effect.

During the first day, a 4-centimetre difference was measured between the water levels above and below the barges. By Saturday morning, the difference had increased to 7–8 centimetres. At the nuclear plant’s cold-water intake, the arrangement had already raised the water level by around one centimetre.

Engineers hope to restore reactor operations

The early results could prove crucial as the Danube continues to fall. Károly Vigh, operations director of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant, said that once the effect of the temporary bottom weir currently being constructed becomes apparent, the reactors will gradually be brought back online.

According to Vigh, Unit 3 will be restarted first, followed by Unit 1. The plant can only return to its nominal maximum output once the water level at the intake has risen by approximately 25 centimetres from its current level.

Emergency intervention aims to prevent further shutdowns

The emergency works are designed to prevent the exceptionally low Danube level from forcing further reductions in the plant’s output. Prime Minister Péter Magyar said on Saturday that without the intervention, the river could fall to a level at which one of the plant’s two currently operating turbines would have to be shut down. A further decline could eventually lead to a complete shutdown.

The government is therefore combining the controlled sinking of the barges with the construction of a temporary bottom weir to raise the river level around the plant. Magyar said the immediate goal was to keep the two remaining operating turbines running and then gradually restore the others once sufficient water levels had been secured.

If you missed it: Hungary begins sinking barges to save Paks NPP and raise critically low Danube levels, PM Magyar receives good news

Political leaders stay away from Paks operation

During his press conference at the site, Magyar also criticised opposition party leaders for not accepting his invitation to visit the emergency works. He said leaders of Fidesz and other parliamentary parties had not attended the briefing and accused them of failing to offer assistance or call for national cooperation.

The prime minister also criticised what he described as misinformation about the situation online. The immediate focus, however, remains on the engineering operation at Paks, where water-management specialists are working against the clock to raise the Danube enough to protect the nuclear plant’s operations.

World.title: Hungary begins sinking barges to save Paks NPP and raise critically low Danube levels, PM Magyar receives good news
World.content:
Hungary has launched an extraordinary emergency operation on the Danube near Paks as authorities race to prevent critically low water levels from affecting the operation of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant.

Two 80-metre barges have been positioned in the river between Paks and Dunaszentbenedek and their controlled sinking has begun. The temporary structures are intended to slow the flow of the Danube and raise water levels around the power plant, producing a similar effect to a low-head weir.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar said on Saturday that the first signs were encouraging: water levels had already risen by one centimetre near the plant’s pumping station.

“This is good news,” Magyar said, while stressing that the situation remains serious.

Water levels threaten reactor operations

The emergency intervention comes as the Danube continues to recede. Water levels at Paks were around -122 centimetres on Saturday, according to Magyar. Current forecasts indicate that the level could fall below -132 centimetres early Monday, a point at which one of the two operating turbines would have to be shut down.

In a more severe scenario, the water level could fall below -140 centimetres, potentially forcing the entire plant to shut down. The government therefore considers preventing a further fall in water levels a priority.

Hundreds of workers and tonnes of rock involved

Around 130 people are currently working directly at the site, while another 50 are involved in administrative tasks. More than 100 lorries are transporting rock to the construction area. Around 5,000 tonnes of rock are expected to arrive during Saturday alone.

The barges have initially been lowered by around 20 centimetres. Eight pumps are being used to bring water into the barges as part of the controlled sinking operation. Meanwhile, work has also begun on both banks of the Danube to construct the temporary structure designed to help raise the river level.

Hungarian military helicopters are also taking part in the operation. Two Airbus H225M helicopters have been used to lift two-tonne concrete blocks brought from Dunakiliti and place them in the river.

National effort mobilised to protect Paks

Magyar said the scale of the emergency justified a broad national effort. Several senior government officials and water-management experts were present at Paks, including Economic and Energy Minister István Kapitány, Minister of Defence Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, Minister heading the Prime Minister’s Office Bálint Ruff and national security adviser Péter Tóth.

Pál Kádár, head of the Defence Administration Office, thanked companies and members of the public who had offered assistance. However, he stressed that the most urgent need was for equipment capable of transporting rock.

Up to 100 lorries may be needed simultaneously on the two sides of the Danube, he said. Magyar added that companies were particularly encouraged to make offers of assistance. The authorities have also warned swimmers and small boats not to approach the work sites because of the serious accident risk.

Operation could determine Paks’s next days

The intervention is being carried out under considerable time pressure. If the river continues to fall as forecast, the first operational threshold could be reached in the early hours of Monday.

The emergency project has already attracted around 150 offers of assistance, according to Magyar.

The government hopes the temporary measures will provide enough of a rise in water levels to keep the power plant operating safely while the Danube remains at exceptionally low levels.

For Hungary, the stakes are high: Paks is the country’s largest nuclear power facility and a key source of domestic electricity. The ongoing operation on the Danube is therefore not simply a major engineering challenge, but an urgent effort to protect the stability of Hungary’s power supply.

World.title: Mysterious cult behind Hungarian murder: Man killed his ex-wife after bitter family dispute – tabloid
World.content:
On the morning of 18 August 1995, a visibly distressed man walked into the police station in Jászberény and told officers to arrest him.

He said he had strangled his wife during an argument at their home in the Hungarian town. However, investigators soon established that the killing had been preceded by months of escalating tension within the family.

At the centre of the conflict was the woman’s involvement with a mysterious religious group, which her husband believed had taken her away from her family. The case would eventually result in a 10-year prison sentence for József Sz. for killing his former wife.

How a religious group tore the family apart

According to Blikk’s account, the couple’s relationship had begun to deteriorate around a year before the murder.

Neighbours recalled that the woman had become increasingly involved with a secretive religious community. She reportedly spent more and more of her time with its members, while her family life was pushed into the background.

Blikk identified the group as the Children of God, an American religious movement whose first Hungarian-speaking group reportedly appeared around Novi Sad (Újvidék), in Serbia, in 1994. The movement allegedly reached the Jászság region several months later, where it was known locally as the Jesus Movement.

The community reportedly imposed strict rules on its members. According to the account, relatives were excluded from membership, only one person from a family could join and married couples were not admitted together. Members were also reportedly expected to abstain from sexual relations with partners or spouses outside the group.

These rules had a profound impact on the family. Neighbours claimed that the woman eventually stopped working and that family savings were being spent on the religious community. Her daughters reportedly complained that their mother was rarely at home.

Husband left the family home

By December 1994, József had had enough. He reportedly left the family home with his daughters and decided to seek a divorce. The divorce was finalised in May 1995, but another dispute soon emerged: who would live in the family home on Kárpát Street?

According to evidence obtained by police, the property had originally belonged to József, who had received it from his parents before his marriage. It therefore was not considered part of the couple’s jointly acquired property. His former wife nevertheless refused to leave.

The final confrontation

On the evening of 17 August 1995, József went to the house to discuss the matter. According to the investigation, he gave his former wife an ultimatum: she should move out before the start of the school year because he and their daughters intended to live there.

He reportedly told her to move in with one of the members of the religious group instead. The woman disagreed. She planned to remain in the property and, according to the account, intended to have a man she had met through the group live there with her.

An argument followed. József turned up the music, reportedly so that neighbours would not be able to hear the dispute. During the ensuing struggle, he grabbed his former wife’s neck and did not let go.

She died from strangulation.

The following morning, József went to the police station and confessed. He was subsequently sentenced to 10 years in prison for the killing.

The Jászberény police station:

What happened to the mysterious group?

The Jesus Movement originated in the United States in the 1970s and grew out of the hippie counterculture. Although it was not a single centrally organised sect, some of its more radical branches later became controversial religious groups.

The movement never became established in Hungary in the same form, according to the account. Some of its followers later became involved with other religious communities, while the group that had caused so much controversy in Jászberény eventually disappeared from the area.

More than three decades later, however, residents around Kárpát Street still remember the extraordinary case, not only because of the murder, but also because of the mysterious religious community that neighbours said had played a role in the breakdown of the family.

World.title: Budget flights are getting expensive: How Ryanair and Wizz Air make money from hidden extras
World.content:
Flying with Europe’s biggest low-cost airlines is becoming significantly more expensive, even though carriers such as Ryanair and Wizz Air are still competing fiercely on headline ticket prices.

An analysis by aviation data provider Cirium found that the selected economy fares of Ryanair, easyJet and Wizz Air were 39.2 per cent higher in May 2026 than a year earlier. Compared with early 2024, average fares had more than doubled.

Importantly, these figures cover the airlines’ basic fares before taxes and external charges. They also exclude many of the extras passengers often end up paying for, such as checked luggage, seat selection and priority boarding.

In other words, the final price of a “cheap” flight can be considerably higher than the advertised fare.

Jet fuel is putting airlines under pressure

The biggest driver behind the rising costs is aviation fuel. According to Világgazdaság, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) expects airlines’ global fuel bill to increase from around $252 billion in 2025 to $350 billion in 2026, representing an increase of almost 40 per cent.

Jet fuel prices surged dramatically in the spring, reaching an average of $188 per barrel in April. Although prices have subsequently fallen, they remain significantly higher than before the latest energy shock.

Airlines cannot simply pass all of these additional costs on to passengers, however. European carriers are also facing increased competition. Cirium data shows that more than 5 per cent more seats are available on intra-European flights this summer. With passengers highly sensitive to prices, airlines have limited room to raise basic fares indefinitely.

The financial results of the low-cost giants demonstrate the pressure. Ryanair’s after-tax profit fell by around a third in the April-June quarter, while its average fares were 6 per cent lower than a year earlier. Wizz Air, meanwhile, reported an operating loss of €183.3 million for the same period.

The real money is increasingly in the extras

So if airlines cannot simply keep raising ticket prices, where does the money come from? Increasingly, it comes from everything outside the basic fare. Baggage, seat selection, priority boarding and other optional services have become crucial sources of revenue for low-cost carriers.

Ryanair generated €4.99 billion from ancillary services in the financial year that ended in March. That worked out at around €24 per passenger and accounted for almost a third of its total €15.54 billion revenue.

The proportion is even higher at Wizz Air. Ancillary services accounted for almost half of the airline’s total revenue in its financial year ending in March 2025. This means that the basic fare is becoming an increasingly incomplete measure of how much a low-cost flight actually costs.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Is the low-cost model changing?

The traditional low-cost model is not disappearing, but it is becoming more complicated for passengers. Someone travelling with only a small amount of luggage, accepting an automatically assigned seat and avoiding additional services can still benefit from a genuinely cheap fare.

But once a passenger adds checked baggage, chooses a particular seat, wants priority boarding or requires other extras, the final bill can move considerably closer to the price charged by a traditional full-service airline. For carriers, meanwhile, ancillary revenue provides a way to keep headline fares relatively competitive while recovering some of their rising costs.

If you missed it: Hungarian Wizz Air opens new base in another European city!

Ryanair and Wizz Air face a delicate balancing act

There is little evidence that the low-cost sector itself is in crisis. Ryanair carried a record 208.4 million passengers in its latest financial year, with a load factor of 94 per cent, while its revenue increased by 11 per cent. The bigger question is how much passengers are willing to pay before the low-cost advantage starts to disappear.

As fuel remains expensive and airlines face rising operating costs, carriers such as Ryanair and Wizz Air are being forced to balance two competing priorities: keeping the advertised fare low enough to attract highly price-sensitive travellers, while generating more revenue from the extras passengers increasingly pay for.

For travellers, it’s important to learn the lesson: the cheapest ticket is not necessarily the cheapest flight. When comparing low-cost fares, the total cost — including luggage, seating and other necessities — is becoming more important than ever.

World.title: Budapest has never seen heatwaves like this: 2026 breaks records twice
World.content:
Both of this year’s extreme heatwaves in Budapest were more intense than ever before, according to an analysis published on the specialist portal Másfélfok (One and a Half Degree) – Climate Change Explained.

Péter Szabó, a climate researcher and PhD student at the meteorology faculty at ELTE, said that Budapest had never before experienced heatwaves like the two that occurred this year.

The first began on 20 June and lasted for 12 days; the second began on 30 July and lasted for 9 days. Although the July heatwave was shorter, it was more intense. On both occasions, it was hotter in the capital than in 2007, when the previous all-time heat record was set.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

The 1994 heatwave also lasted 12 days, but it was nowhere near as intense as the two this year, Szabó said. Although the heatwave in July 2024 was the longest, lasting 13 days, it was less intense than the one at the start of August this year.

He added that for several decades in the 20th century, moderately intense heatwaves occurred every few years, followed by a longer period during which no heatwaves developed. However, after 1990, the effects of climate change became apparent, and it was really only after 2010 that heatwaves became prolonged and intense. During the hottest summer, in 2024, a total of around 1,300 more people died over the course of three weeks of heatwaves, meaning that excess mortality stood at nearly 20 percent nationwide.

World.title: Mystery solved: Here’s which unit the WWII German motorcycle found in the Danube was linked to – photos
World.content:
A Second World War-era military motorcycle discovered in the muddy bed of the Danube in Budapest has now been identified as belonging to a specific German military unit.

The motorcycle emerged from the heavily receding river near Batthyány Square earlier this month. Experts from the Hungarian Ministry of Defence’s Institute and Museum of Military History have determined that it once served with the armoured engineer battalion of the German Feldherrnhalle (FHH) Panzer Division.

The identification was made possible by markings painted on the motorcycle’s storage box, according to Norbert Számvéber, director of the Institute’s Military History Archives and Map Collection.

Clues hidden on the bike

The markings indicate that the motorcycle originally belonged to the unit when it was still known as Pionier-Bataillon Feldherrnhalle.

The unit was reorganised in September 1944 and renamed Panzer-Pionier-Bataillon Feldherrnhalle by the end of September or, at the latest, early October. However, the motorcycle still bears the earlier “Pi. Btl.” abbreviation, suggesting that it may have joined the unit in September, before the name change.

Military historians also examined the tactical marking found on the motorcycle. As it has no number and the left-hand edge of the branch insignia is not thickened (a feature that would have indicated one of the companies), experts believe the motorcycle most likely served with the battalion headquarters.

What was the Feldherrnhalle unit?

The Feldherrnhalle formations had a long and complex history within Nazi Germany’s armed forces. The unit that ultimately became part of the Feldherrnhalle Panzer Division fought on both the Eastern Front and in Hungary during the Second World War.

The armoured engineer battalion was responsible for tasks including mine-laying and mine clearance, constructing and overcoming obstacles, bridge-building and demolishing military installations. It could also be used as an assault formation in fortified and urban combat.

Parts of the Feldherrnhalle formation arrived in Hungary in 1944, including during the German occupation of the country. Elements of the division were later involved in the fighting in and around Budapest.

The newly identified motorcycle therefore offers another small but tangible link to the military history of Budapest during the final stages of the Second World War.

Its discovery was made possible by the unusually low water level of the Danube, which has recently exposed a number of objects and structures normally hidden beneath the river.

World.title: Budapest braces for major traffic restrictions starting Saturday ahead of 20 August celebrations
World.content:
Budapest motorists and pedestrians should prepare for major traffic restrictions from this Saturday as the city gears up for Hungary’s 20 August national holiday celebrations. According to the Budapest Police Headquarters (BRFK), road closures and other restrictions will remain in place until 25 August.

Several key roads, bridges and public spaces will be affected, with the Chain Bridge and Margaret Bridge among the locations facing closures.

Traffic restrictions begin this Saturday

According to a statement published on police.hu, partial closures will begin on Saturday, affecting, among other areas, Műegyetem Quay and several sections of both the Buda and Pest lower quays. In the Buda Castle District, parts of Szentháromság Street and Tárnok Street will also be closed to traffic.

Chain Bridge to close from Sunday morning

The Chain Bridge will be closed to motor traffic from 6 AM on Sunday. From 7 AM, both the northern and southern pavements will also be closed to pedestrians. These restrictions will remain in place until noon on 21 August.

The Margaret Bridge will also be affected on Sunday. From 9 PM, one lane on the northern side of the bridge will be closed. From 10 PM, both pavements will be closed to pedestrians. These restrictions are likewise expected to remain until noon on 21 August.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

More closures coming next week

From next Tuesday, motorists can expect restrictions on sections of Zoltán Street, Nádor Street and Akadémia Street, as well as on Műegyetem Quay.

On Wednesday, Várkert Quay will be closed along its entire length. In the evening, restrictions will also be introduced on Kós Károly Promenade, between Heroes’ Square and Állatkerti Boulevard, and on Széchenyi Quay, between Kossuth Square and Széchenyi Square. Salkaházi Sára Quay will also be affected.

Full Margaret Bridge closure on 20 August

On 20 August, Hungary’s national holiday, further restrictions will come into force across the capital. Among other locations, Szent István Square will be closed, while the entire Margaret Bridge will also be inaccessible. Later that evening, motorists will face another major restriction: the Elisabeth Bridge will be closed to motor traffic between 7 PM and 11 PM.

With preparations for Budapest’s 20 August celebrations already beginning, residents and visitors are advised to plan their journeys carefully and allow extra time for travel across the capital.

World.title: Man attacks two Hungarian police officers and service dog, officers use tear gas to stop him – video
World.content:
A man in his twenties has been arrested in Hungary after allegedly attacking two police officers and a service dog during an incident at his home in Komárom-Esztergom County.

The man was reportedly behaving aggressively and damaging property inside his home when police were called to the scene. He was subsequently detained on suspicion of violence against a public official and attempted grievous bodily harm. A court ordered his detention on Friday following a motion by the Győr Regional Investigative Prosecutor’s Office, the Hungarian News Agency reported.

Man attacked officers and police dog

Four police officers arrived at the man’s home and told him that he would be taken to hospital by ambulance for a medical examination. However, the man allegedly refused to cooperate and instead became aggressive towards the officers and the service dog deployed at the scene.

Despite being ordered to stop, he allegedly punched two officers several times, kicked one of them twice and also attacked the service dog. Police eventually managed to restrain him by using tear gas before handcuffing him. He reportedly continued to resist even after being detained.

Two officers injured

The confrontation left two police officers injured. One suffered a head injury and bruising to the hip, while the other sustained a skull contusion. A specialised unit from the Győr-Moson-Sopron County Police Headquarters and Hungary’s National Protective Service also assisted with the arrest at the request of the investigative prosecutor’s office.

The suspect was taken into custody and questioned as a suspect but did not make a statement. He did not file a complaint against the charges brought against him.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Suspect previously convicted of drug offences

The case is being treated particularly seriously because the man had previously been convicted several times of drug-related offences. According to prosecutors, he allegedly attacked the police while still serving the probationary period of a suspended prison sentence.

The offences he is suspected of committing – taking the applicable cumulative sentencing rules into account – carry a potential prison sentence of between one and seven and a half years. The investigative prosecutor therefore requested his detention, arguing that the circumstances justified the measure. The court granted the request on Friday.

The investigation into violence against a public official and attempted grievous bodily harm is ongoing.

World.title: Romanian swimmer David Popovici claims third European 200m freestyle title after 100m triumph
World.content:
Romanian swimming star David Popovici has won the 200m freestyle race at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, his third consecutive European title in the event.

The win on August 14, following the August 12 gold in the 100m freestyle race, makes him the only athlete to have won both races at three consecutive editions of the European championships.

The 21-year-old Romanian swimmer finished the race with a time of 1:44.15, 0.40 seconds ahead of runner-up Tomas Navikonis of Lithuania, and 0.72 seconds ahead of Britain's James Guy.

In the 200m freestyle event, Popovici also won the Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, as well as two world titles, in Budapest in 2022 and in Singapore in 2025.

His personal best in the 200m freestyle came at the 2022 European Championships, when he clocked 1:42.97, the third-fastest time in history.

World.title: Romanian executive to submit fifth payment request under Recovery and Resilience Facility
World.content:
The Romanian government is set to submit the fifth payment request under the EU-backed Recovery and Resilience Facility, or PNRR, according to an announcement from European Investments and Projects minister Dragoș Pîslaru.

Payment no. 5 is worth EUR 2.84 billion, and is the penultimate request that Romania will submit within the PNRR. Once approved, the fifth payment will bring Romania’s absorption rate of PNRR-related grants to 78%, from 66% currently.

“One final request remains, request no. 6, worth EUR 2.58 billion in grants and EUR 1.76 billion in loans. From a total of EUR 13.57 billion allocated at the time the PNRR was signed, we will reach EUR 10.56 billion after request no. 5,” Pîslaru said during a press conference.

Initially, the European Commission planned for a single final payment request, reuniting the now separated requests no. 5 and 6, the minister noted.

The final payment request will be submitted at the end of September, and with it “we could reach 97.2% of the PNRR,” he said, referring to the grants component.

“47% was the percentage of the PNRR when I came to the ministry, after four years since the program was launched. The annual average was about 10.4% of the PNRR. In one year and two months, under the Bolojan government, we added 31% of the PNRR,” the minister also said.

Romania’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan is financed through EUR 21.41 billion under the EU mechanism, including EUR 13.57 billion in grants and EUR 7.84 billion in loans. The fourth payment request, worth EUR 2.62 billion, was approved by the European Commission in May of this year.
